canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across the papers, the prevailing usage treats Conscientiousness as a Big Five personality trait. The clearest definition describes it as characterized by diligence, organization, and self-discipline, and one source snippet similarly associates it with diligence and carefulness. A narrower framing keeps the trait-based view but focuses on its positive aspect, associating it with detailed explanations and improvement in tasks when positively activated.

Space of facets. Papers place Conscientiousness alongside openness, extraversion or extroversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism as one of the Big Five personality dimensions. One line of work further isolates a positive aspect of Conscientiousness in terms of neurons associated with that aspect.

Space of measurement. No measurement instrument is linked to Conscientiousness, and no behavioral indicator is linked to it. The only explicit measurement description says that a paper uses the IPIP-NEO-120 questionnaire to quantify behavior patterns across the five personality dimensions, including Conscientiousness, so the available operationalization is questionnaire-based rather than attached to a recorded linked instrument or indicator.

Links. No causal, correlational, or other related links are recorded for Conscientiousness.
